thesis: Allegion plc (NYSE: ALLE) is a global provider of security and access-control products for commercial and residential buildings. **[Fact]** The company sells mechanical and electronic locks, door closers, exit devices, access-control software, and related services under brands including Schlage, Von Duprin, LCN, and SimonsVoss. **[Fact]** FY2025 net revenue was **$4.07 billion**, up from **$3.77 billion** in 2024 and **$3.65 billion** in 2023. **[Fact]** FY2025 net earnings were **$643.8 million** (**$7.48** basic EPS) on **$859.5 million** operating income. **[Fact]** Cash from operations was **$783.8 million** in 2025. **[Inference]** Allegion earns when architects, contractors, and building owners specify its hardware and electronic access platforms; the mix is shifting toward electronics and software while mechanical security remains the cash engine.
why_market_wrong: The market may be pricing Allegion as a fully compounding quality industrial at **$138.13**, while underweighting **$1.98 billion long-term debt** against **$356 million** cash (roughly **$19 per share** net debt drag in the component contract) and **non-residential construction cyclicality**. **[Inference]** FY2025 Americas non-residential revenue grew high-single digits on price and volume, but residential revenue fell low-single digits on volume; a construction downturn would compress volumes before pricing power fully offsets. The component schedule prices a **-$6 per share** construction-cycle reserve for this reason. **[Inference]** Electronic access and software mix is a reinvestment runway (**+$8 per share** base component), but the market may already embed much of that in the multiple at **~17 times** trailing owner cash.
